user_inputs.input: You are to create a canvas plugin targeted towards GLP-1 prescribed patient care gaps. This will not take over the care itself, but act as a copilot for professionals monitoring and taking actions on their patients. The plugin initializes when a clinician opens a note or opens the patient's chart. The patient being patients prescribed glp-1 agonist or with a documented obesity-related condition. The plugin will access the canvas data module to pull the following: current meds, most recent weight/BMI vitals, last visit date, labs (it will use reasoning to output relevant labs). The plugin will flag gaps in the queried information like no weight logging in a clinically appropriate window (configurable, default 30 days), if the patient is overdue for labs before next dose increase, or if the patient does not have a follow up appointment scheduled. All thresholds should be configurable rather than hardcoded. The plugin will create a card in the patient's chart with action buttons: create staff outreach task, or inject commands like ordering the missing lab for the patient. These actions only occur on explicit clinician click, the plugin never creates tasks or injects commands automatically; it surfaces information and lets the clinician decide. Before re-flagging or creating a new outreach task, the plugin should check whether an existing open task for the same gap already exists on the patient and avoid duplicating it. The top of the card will have a short rationale non-actionable outputted response, generated by an LLM based on the queried information, e.g. for an example patient: "8 weeks overdue for weight check per titration protocol." Essentially it will be a quick summary when the card generates to get the clinician up to speed with their patient. When constructing the LLM prompt for this rationale, pass only the minimal derived facts needed (e.g. weeks overdue, which labs are missing, gap type) rather than raw patient-identifying information, to keep PHI exposure to the LLM call to a minimum.
Yes go ahead with the spec, and here is the remote for the repo: https://github.com/EdwardPunzalan/glp1-care-gap-copilot.git
